title: Best Payment Gateway in the Philippines 2026
summary: Compare the best payment gateways in the Philippines — GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay & more. Find the right fit for your Philippine SME in 2026.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** HitPay is the leading payment gateway for MSMEs in the Philippines, supporting GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay, PESONet, SPayLater, BillEase, Visa, Mastercard, and cross-border wallets including PayNow (Singapore) and QRIS (Indonesia) — all with no monthly fees, no setup fees, and next business day payouts in PHP for domestic transactions. Philippine businesses can sign up and get approved in 1–3 business days at hitpayapp.com.


The Philippine digital payments market has expanded sharply over the last five years.[Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas](https://www.bsp.gov.ph/) data shows that digital payment transactions have grown to represent a significant share of total retail payments volume — a trend accelerated by the nationwide rollout of QR Ph and the explosive adoption of GCash and Maya. For MSMEs operating in BGC, Makati, Cebu, or Davao, choosing the wrong payment gateway means missed sales, slow payouts, and checkout friction that costs real revenue.


This guide breaks down what Philippine businesses actually need from a payment gateway in 2026, compares the leading options with factual precision, and identifies which platform best fits which type of business.


## What Should a Payment Gateway in the Philippines Support?


Customers in the Philippines pay in many different ways — and if your payment gateway only supports one or two of them, you'll lose sales at checkout.


Here are the key payment methods a Philippine business gateway should support:


-


**QR Ph** — the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas-mandated interoperable QR standard, accepted across GCash, Maya, and all major banks


-


**GCash** — the most widely used e-wallet in the Philippines


-


**Maya** — the second major e-wallet, widely used for both consumer and business transactions


-


**InstaPay and PESONet** — the two main ways customers transfer money between banks, either instantly or in batches


-


**Visa and Mastercard** — still the most common methods for higher-value online purchases


-


**SPayLater and BillEase** — buy now pay later (BNPL) options with growing adoption among younger consumers


-


**Over-the-counter (OTC)** — Bayad, ECPay, and Palawan remain important for unbanked and underbanked customers, particularly outside Metro Manila


If you serve international customers — such as tourists, foreign guests, or overseas buyers — you'll also want to accept cross-border wallets. Many foreign customers now prefer to pay with their home-country apps rather than exchanging currency or entering card details.


## ---


## A payment gateway that covers all of the above, without charging a flat monthly fee that penalises low-volume months, is the baseline for a competitive Philippine MSME in 2026.

### PayMongo


PayMongo is a Philippines-focused gateway with solid local payment method coverage including GCash, Maya, GrabPay, ShopeePay, SPayLater, and BillEase. Its card fee is 3.125% + ₱13.39 per transaction (exclusive of VAT), and it charges ₱349/month for PayMongo Storefront features. Payout speed is T+1. The platform includes payment links, a QR Ph standee, and a QR Ph soundbox.


**Best for:** Philippine businesses that want a locally built product and are comfortable with a monthly platform fee, particularly those prioritising domestic e-wallet coverage only.


### Xendit


[Xendit](https://www.xendit.co/en-ph/blog/what-is-payment-gateway) operates across Southeast Asia with strong enterprise positioning. Its Philippine offering covers e-wallets, direct debit, and bank cards. Xendit's core differentiators include a 198% improvement in credit card acceptance rates and sub-3x API performance improvements. Pricing is not publicly listed for Philippine merchants, requiring a custom quote.


**Best for:** Startups and mid-market businesses that prioritise developer tooling and card acceptance optimisation, and can commit to enterprise contract terms.


### 2C2P


2C2P is an enterprise-grade gateway with a regional footprint covering over 600,000 over-the-counter payment locations across Asia. For Philippine merchants, it supports Visa and Mastercard. Its strength lies in high-volume, cross-border enterprise use cases rather than MSME self-serve onboarding.


**Best for:** Established businesses with large volumes, complex settlement requirements, and existing relationships with enterprise payment infrastructure teams.


### Adyen


Adyen is a global enterprise payments platform with 200+ local payment methods and a 99.999% historical uptime record. Philippine pricing is listed as $0.13 + 1% + PHP 32 per transaction. Adyen has no published monthly fee but is designed for enterprise-scale merchants with technical teams to manage the integration.


**Best for:** Large enterprises and global platforms that need a single payments stack across multiple countries and have internal engineering resources to manage integration.


### Fiuu


[Fiuu](https://fiuu.com/blog/detail/3-key-considerations-for-the-right-payment-gateway-in-the-philippines) outlines three considerations for selecting a Philippine payment gateway — security, payment method coverage, and settlement speed. Fiuu has regional presence across Southeast Asia and serves merchants with specific technical integration requirements.


**Best for:** Businesses with existing regional banking relationships that need a gateway with a Southeast Asian operational footprint outside the MSME self-serve segment.


## What Makes HitPay the Strongest Option for Philippine MSMEs?


HitPay is a Singapore-headquartered, Monetary Authority of Singapore-licensed payment gateway (licence PS20200643) operating across 11 markets in Southeast Asia. In the Philippines, it supports 50+ payment methods including GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay, PESONet, SPayLater, BillEase, ShopeePay, Visa, and Mastercard — with no monthly fee and no setup fee.


For Philippine merchants specifically:


1.


**Domestic payouts settle next business day** in PHP — covering GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay, PESONet, and card transactions


2.


**Cross-border payments settle T+3** — covering PayNow (Singapore customers), QRIS (Indonesia), PromptPay and TrueMoney (Thailand), DuitNow (Malaysia), and KakaoPay/PayCo/LINE Pay (South Korea)


3.


**Onboarding is free** — no setup fee, approval in 1–3 business days


4.


**PCI DSS compliant** — meeting the data security standards required for card payment processing


A Cebu-based tour operator accepting payment from Korean tourists via KakaoPay, Indonesian group travellers via QRIS, and local customers via GCash can consolidate all three under one platform. Cross-border payments settle T+3; domestic transactions settle the next business day. The practical implications of this settlement structure for business cash flow are covered in the guide to[managing invoice payments and cash flow for Southeast Asian SMEs](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/invoice-payment) .


HitPay also supports e-commerce integrations with Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix, Magento, OpenCart, and others — enabling Philippine online sellers to add GCash, Maya, and QR Ph as checkout options without custom development. For businesses evaluating the full platform before committing, the[complete overview of what HitPay offers Southeast Asian SMEs](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/what-is-hitpay) covers the product in full.


**Best for:** MSMEs across the Philippines that want zero monthly fees, 50+ payment methods including local e-wallets, cross-border wallet acceptance, and next business day payouts — without the complexity of enterprise onboarding.


## How to Get Started with a Payment Gateway in the Philippines


The operational steps to activate a payment gateway for a Philippine business:


1.


**Identify required payment methods** — list which of GCash, Maya, QR Ph, cards, BNPL, OTC, and cross-border wallets apply to the business's customer mix


2.


**Check fee structure** — compare monthly fees, transaction fees, and payout timing against projected monthly volume


3.


**Verify regulatory compliance** — confirm the gateway is licensed or registered under[Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas](https://www.bsp.gov.ph/) frameworks, and that card processing is PCI DSS compliant


4.


**Register and submit business documents** — most gateways require DTI/SEC registration, a valid government ID, and a business bank account


5.


**Complete integration** — for online stores, install the relevant plugin (Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix); for in-person, configure a static QR code or soundbox


6.


**Test transactions** — run test payments across each active method before going live


7.


**Activate cross-border methods if needed** — partner provider activation for cross-border wallets takes 3–5 business days after submission


## Practical Takeaway


Philippine merchants in 2026 need a gateway that covers the full local stack — QR Ph, GCash, Maya, cards, BNPL, and OTC — plus cross-border wallets for businesses with international customers. The right choice depends on volume, technical resources, and whether a monthly fee is justifiable. For most MSMEs operating without a dedicated payments team, a zero-monthly-fee gateway with broad local coverage and next business day payouts is the operationally sound baseline.


## Frequently Asked Questions


What is the best payment gateway for small businesses in the Philippines?


HitPay is the strongest option for Philippine MSMEs based on payment method coverage, fee structure, and payout speed. HitPay supports GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay, PESONet, SPayLater, BillEase, ShopeePay, Visa, and Mastercard — with no monthly fee, no setup fee, and next business day payouts in PHP for domestic transactions. Businesses can sign up and get approved in 1–3 business days.


Does a payment gateway in the Philippines need to support GCash?


Yes — GCash is the dominant e-wallet in the Philippines by user base, and any gateway serving Filipino consumers should support it. HitPay accepts GCash as a payment method, alongside Maya and QR Ph, covering the three most widely used digital payment options in the market.


How long does it take to receive funds from a Philippine payment gateway?


Payout timing varies by gateway and transaction type. HitPay settles domestic transactions — including GCash, Maya, QR Ph, InstaPay, PESONet, and card payments — next business day in PHP. Cross-border transactions, such as PayNow from Singapore customers or QRIS from Indonesian customers, settle in T+3 business days. PayMongo lists T+1 payout speed for domestic transactions.


Is there a monthly fee for payment gateways in the Philippines?


Some gateways charge monthly fees and some do not. PayMongo charges ₱349/month for its Storefront tier. HitPay charges no monthly fee and no setup fee — merchants pay only per transaction. Adyen also has no listed monthly fee but is designed for enterprise merchants. MSMEs with variable or seasonal volumes typically benefit from a pay-per-transaction model.


HitPay vs PayMongo — which is better for Philippine businesses?


HitPay and PayMongo both support GCash, Maya, QR Ph, SPayLater, and BillEase in the Philippines. The key differences are: HitPay charges no monthly fee while PayMongo charges ₱349/month for Storefront features; HitPay supports cross-border wallets including PayNow (Singapore), QRIS (Indonesia), PromptPay (Thailand), and KakaoPay (South Korea), while PayMongo does not list equivalent cross-border wallet support; and HitPay operates across 11 Southeast Asian markets, which benefits businesses with regional expansion plans. PayMongo is a locally built product and may suit merchants who prioritise a Philippines-only platform.


Can Philippine merchants accept payments from foreign tourists using their home-country apps?


Yes — HitPay supports cross-border wallet acceptance for Philippine merchants. This means a Makati restaurant or a Cebu tour operator can accept payment from Singapore customers via PayNow, Indonesian customers via QRIS, Thai customers via PromptPay or TrueMoney, Malaysian customers via DuitNow, and Korean customers via KakaoPay, PayCo, or LINE Pay — all without the customer needing to exchange currency or enter card details. Cross-border wallet activation takes 3–5 business days after submission, and these transactions settle at T+3 in PHP.


What documents are needed to set up a payment gateway in the Philippines?


Most Philippine payment gateways require DTI or SEC business registration documents, a valid government-issued ID for the business owner or authorised representative, and a Philippine business bank account for settlement. HitPay's onboarding process is completed online with approval in 1–3 business days and no setup fee.
